This game had a lot of promise and it was overall a huge let down. The story as far as I know is there is a black knight who wipes our the dragons and it's your job to hatch, grow up and fight the black knight. Well, an hour into the game I was given what I assume it the boss fight. This is the second boss fight, I've only had one dragon friend in my brood(though the screenshots show having more) and he gets killed RIGHT before this fight happens. The fight itself is EXCRUCIATINGLY difficult. I'm talking a HUGE jump in difficulty compared to the rest of the game.
The first part of the fight is so small and cramped that more often then not you'll get locked into a corner and get killed, and since the flight mechanics aren't great you often miss the rocks you have to smash or don't trigger the smash at all. The second part of the fight only offers you two goblins (worth two hearts each) for food, but you're going to lose easily two hearts if the enemy gets close and will often find stopping to eat these guys puts you in more danger. You can't melee fight this guy because his sword attacks hit ridiculously fast, he jumps around just as fast as you do, summons random ghosts (literally random spawning, I had one spawn IN me during the fight) that have a very far flight path that you have to dodge, he has an AOE that has a very large range and fires arrows at you. The only tactic I had to fight this guy was run at him and chomp away while he summoned ghosts.
THEN, after taking him down to NO health, he turns to a ghost and flies around JUST AS FAST as you and non-stop melee's. I assume it's a 'survive long enough to espace' kind of deal, but it's a small arena with barely any room to stop and recharge your flight long enough to keep away from him.
This could have been a really cute adorable game if it were longer, had at least one or two more companions and boss fights that let you bring those companions in to the fight. I mean, the trailer even said I'd need to protect my dragons but I didn't even get the chance to. Directly after he ran off to get his fire breathe, we went into the boss fight.

Disclosure: This game was provided as a review code directly from the developer.
Dragon's Wake has serious style. It's short, and sweet, and simple, and utterly charming. Throwing players into a world of a baby dragon, it sets you on a journey of discovery, growth, and loss.
A platformer, players gain various abilities throughout the game, developing the ability to glide, breath fire, and even spit fireballs. Gliding takes a little bit to get used to, as the game doesn't really describe it very well, but once understood, it provides a very mobile and very frantic mode of travel.
As a dragon, you have a variety of attacks. You can bite, stomp, and breath fire, and all three allow the player to take down enemies in a variety of ways. Combat's light, but as it's not the main focus of the game, it doesn't need to be heavier.
Artistically, Dragon's Wake is, again, simple. It's pixel art, but details everything very well. Each character has, well, character, and provides just enough to be able to make distinctions in a characters emotion.
Dragon's Wake has heart, and while short, it delivers a powerful story from start to finish. In the hour that it takes to finish the game, you'll encounter loss and heartbreak, but also victory. I didn't realise it while playing through, but every loss seems to be avoidable, providing replayability.
I really enjoyed my short time with Dragon's Wake, and for a game that one person made over two years, I think it's very much worth checking out.

But even with other control schemes, "balance", "grip", there is only one way to take corners with any speed:  Drifting.
And even this wouldn't be as bad if it had the same more realistic drifting controls as the previous game.  But this game doesn't.  Not by a long shot.  While it may be better than the infamously bad Ridge Racer series, Codemasters has decided to throw away all pretense of a "racing simulator" and give us crappy arcade drifting physics.  Every car will under-steer unless you hit the breaks to throw the back end out.  Every.  Single.  Car.  Every track is made for drifting around sharp bends.  Every race expect you to drift if you want any sort of reasonable time.  Simply put, if you aren't drifting, you aren't winning.
On top of that, the career tournament, sponsor, money/reputation system of the previous game is gone.  Replaced with a "social media" story, complete with ESPN interludes (who've proven they will do anything for a pay check whether it has any sense of reality or not).  You win races to earn "fans" (reputation).  Cars are just given to you, you choose between usually two - which are either virtually identical in stats or one will be a clear advantage - and you can unlock the other in a time trial.  The goal of the game is to impress drivers from other racing circuits to join your racing circuit by beating them in races.  Let me put that another way:  The goal is to impress enough fans that your brand new, all-styles racing circuit is totally for realsies by attracting drivers that you, personally, have bested in their own circuits, on their own tracks, against their own specialties.  And now you want to race them off type, off class, and against each other to give credibility for your fantasy league.  Yea, this is so much better than just, you know, trying to earn trophies from existing events.
On top of that, the AI has taken a huge step back from the previous game.  Whereas in previous game, drivers had skill sets, they had favorite types, and - most importantly - they made mistakes, here we are back to AI that was laughable twenty years ago.  They follow their racing line.  They drive a little slower if they're out front, so that you can catch up, and a little faster if they're behind you (rubber band AI).  They don't care if they hit a wall, they don't care if you're in the way, they don't care if you try to spin them.  They will stick to their racing line and that is it.
But wait, there's more.  In their infinite wisdom, Codemasters has added a few new race types, and of course removed some old favorites.  One of the new events, Live Routes, is a race track that is dynamically altered as you race.  In other words, you have to picture that there are people who, once a few cars go buy, run out and reset the direction of the track.  Constantly.  In a game filled with unrealistic, idiotic choices, this one takes the cake.
Edit:  There is also the dreaded, obsolete, should not be seen in any video game post 2000 checkpoint racing.  This was a mechanic invented for arcade machines back when you had to continually put quarters in them every 90 seconds in order for them to earn money.  You have a time limit, and each checkpoint adds a little bit to it - not enough to get to the next point on its own, so that you will eventually run out.  It has absolutely no place in home games.  This mechanic needs to die.  Even though it is used here slightly differently than in the old arcade games, here it's set up as an actual competetion - which is probably the best use you can make out of it - checkpoint racing has left such a dirty taste in my mouth from so many games that I just cannot respect any racing game that includes it anymore.  This isn't the only thing either.  Elimination, the way they have the "5 second rule" to Togue.  This game has completely forgone "simulation" for "arcade".  While some players may like that, having race styles that can only really be done IN a video game... After the first GRID game, this is not at all what I wanted to see in the sequel.  I have no problem if that's the game that they wanted to make... but it should not be titled GRID 2.
There are better racing games out there.  If you haven't already played the first GRID, go give that one a shot.  The cars there feel good, the game looks good, the races make sense, the AI is competitive, and most importantly, that game is far more FUN.  But hey, at least you can have pearlescent paint if you buy this one instead - though you can never remove your sponsors.

Ever since I first heard of
I was excited. I am a huge stealth-fan and I never got around to playing the original
-games, so this was a great opportunity for me and other newcomers to jump right into this iconic stealth series... and I am very glad that I did.
is a beautiful game and a unique stealth experience with smooth gameplay and lots of variety in your approach on things. Simply a superb game that is unfortunately brought down by critics and die-hards fan who expected something that would have stuck more to the "original recipe".
The Good:
· Smooth controls: climbing low obstacles, peeking around corners to get a better look at your environment, swooping from shadow to shadow... It all feels incredibly smooth, especially for a stealth game. If you have ever played
, just imagine something like that without magic and a more realistic approach.
· Money money money: getting your gold-greedy paws around precious items such as common goblets and letter openers among countless others and more unique collectable items is incredibly fun and satisfying. This loot is generally realistically spread, meaning no golden goblets will be found on the streets and that jewelry will mostly be found in stores or houses. I personally think this encouraged me to explore different area's to find different kind of loot.
· Phenomenal stealth gameplay: there are no stealth games this well-crafted in my recent memory. Your approach may depend on the situation, your goal or the difficulty (which is geniously customizable to enjoy the game as hard or as simple as you'd like). You can sneak past every guard, knock them all out, just steal all their money (heheh), or you can distract guards by firing arrows, putting out fires, throwing empty bottles etc. It feels fresh and addictive and completely different with every level or replay.
The Bad:
· AI: there's dumb AI and there's blind AI. I'd say the AI isn't necessarily dumb (birds and dogs will alert guards and guard frequently and correctly patrol the area) but the AI is blind as f*ck. Alright, you're in the shadows, but at times you can literally walk in front of guards and they'll keep their eyes fixed on you, but they won't react. This idiocy encouraged me to stay as far away from guars as possible, but I'd prefer my AI a little bit more alert and responsive.
· Pure stealth may not be for everyone: in games like
or
you can either go in pure stealth without ever being noticed of going in a bit more fierce, killing every enemy in sight. You can obviously kill enemies with an arrow in between the enemy's eyes, but real action is avoided. The more stealthy you play, the more rewarding (both in-game and personally) and immersive the game will be, but poor in-game combat will put off almost everyone looking to cause some fuss.
The Ugly:
· Man this game is gorgeous. Amazing textures, immersive lighting, stunning character models, an atmospheric city and espacially Garrett's hands are detailed beyond belief. One of the most beautiful games in recent memory.
Final Verdict:
·
is not for everyone due to its imperfections, but for stealth-fans like myself this game is a must. It's the very best stealth has to offer and undoubtedly a game that will stick with you for a long time. 9.5/10

It all happened on a cold winter night. My shelter was running low on fuel, and running low on fuel meant that I couldn't boil some water. Running low on fuel meant that I couldn't cook any food. Running low on fuel meant that I wouldn't be able to keep warm throughout the night. Running low on fuel would be the cause of my death if I did not do anything about it.
I had foolishly used up the majority of my fuel and wood beforehand, not preparing for the harshness of winter. Everyone on the streets of Sarajevo valued those two items more than gold itself - and rightly so. Being able to keep warm means not getting sick and trading away all of your goods for that bottle of medicine, afterall.
I had heard of a semi-detached house. Some thugs were living in one part, but the other was completely abandoned. I thought I could sneak on through and gather  what I needed to survive the winter, but I was wrong. I was spotted by a girl and she immediately opened fire on me. I bolted for the exit, managing to stay alive but now I was wounded.
I would not let her make a fool of me!
The very next night, I sent another survivor in. This time, I was armed with a knife and a mission. I was going to wipe that building clear of these lunatics so that they can't hurt anyone else. I was able to find myself a nice hiding spot and lured the shooter into a trap. As the frail girl creeped by me, shotgun in hand, I lunged out and stabbed her. She fell over, and I continued to stab until she stopped moving.
I turned around to find one of her friends behind me, watching as I sunk the blade of my knife in and pulling it back out repeatedly. I prepared myself to fight this new enemy, but she just dropped to her knees and bawled her eyes out. I was stunned as two other girls came running out and completely broke down in front of me.
I had helped cover for a neighbor from the militia. I had given some brave children my only bottle of medicine and two cans of food when I had hungry people of my own. I had gone out to help people trapped under rubble. I ran through a street covered by a sniper just to help an injured man get back to his infant child. I thought I could still keep my humanity in this horrible war, that I could hold onto this ideal that people are inherently good.
But I had become a monster.

Really nice game, what I was expecting.
A simple, yet fun, and challenging, but fair, straightforward, relatively short, but complete, game.
It follows a very distinctive premise, like the one you’ve come to expect from a cartoon you’re basically trying to climb up the floors of a tower ruled by an evil man, each of the floors is a stage that is composed of different sections.
Each of them being unique, and exclusive in their design.
For the most part you’re simply going to be fighting a series of enemies, you die in a single hit, but luckily, the game respawns you instantly, at the start of each section that you’re in.
For the most part it’s not frustrating but after a while it turns into a bit of an slog, in later levels, when you’re going through massive sections that can last more than ten minutes or so depending on how experienced, or familiar, you are with the game mechanics.
It always felt fair though, and usually in the moments in which I would start getting frustrated, I would just simply end up beating a particular area that was giving me problems after a couple of more tries.
At the most I must have died 30, or so, times in only a few selections of levels.
It is worth it though, because the game, while being incredibly simplistic, it is truly an enjoyable experience.
The combat system allows you to punch your enemies, pickup weapons that you can either use as bludgeon objects against your enemies, effectively covering a wider are than you will with your regular attack, paired with the ability to throw said weapon by simply “clicking” the “B” button, you can also throw the melee weapons, so in a way they’re preferable, but all of them are distinctive and good, you can find them scattered around the sections of the levels you’re in, or, at times, destroy objects that provide you with them.
The combat system its incredibly satisfying, the overall feel of the chain of attacks you can create with not only the weapons that you get, but by simply attacking the enemies just with your fists, it’s very responsive, and provide me with a clear feeling of empowerment.
The biggest, and most unique aspect of the game, however, lies within its “shifting” ability, basically you can teleport around the sections of the game.
It is a really useful ability in combat and gives the game an incredibly unique feel to it.
It is however something that’s limited, and that you can only use a couple of times up until it needs time to regenerate, I have no problem with this, is an important way to maintain, and give the game balance, the only issue that I have with it is that if you exhaust all of your “shifting power” you need to wait more, than if you just stop, right before you use all of it.
It is annoying because at times I would die just from my own poor management of my ability, rather than because I actually made a mistake by ending up right in front of an enemy.
This few times felt a bit frustrating, as I felt somewhat “cheated” of some attempts, based on an unnecessary restriction imposed right on top of one that is necessary.
It was a minor “dent” however, and for the rest of the game, and even in the times I would die from it, I would just laugh it off, but it is redundant in my opinion, and something that should’ve been left as just a regular recharge, rather than punish, or motivate the player to scrutinize its “shifting meter” even further.
Overall, in my 2 hours and a half I enjoyed the game thoroughly, I thought it was a fun, and enjoyable experience, that was challenging, yet filled with small lines of dialog that provide the characters with just the right amount of charisma for me to find them memorable and enjoyable.
Totally recommend it.

When you build up your collection of nuts and bolts, then you can upgrade and get a third jump - which makes things a bit easier.
Always head right.
Press space to jump.
Don't miss the planets.
Watch out for the flaming asteroids.
There are 40 goals to achieve.
Unfortunately, only a maximum of three goals are active at any one time. I would have preferred to have the entire forty available. The limiting of goal availability is a bit painful.

Frog Climbers is a new indie game made by a team of four called TeamCrew and published by Plug In Digital. The game began production back in March of 2015, where it went on to win best execution in design and gamer's choice award. It is now set to release on steam on October 6th.
The game is a local multiplayer party game made for up to four players. That's right local, there is no online play whatsoever... unless you count the leader board times when you are playing the solo daily speedruns. Having no online component does seem to kill the playtime when playing with friends. I brought a few of my friends over to play the game and test out how well we would do. While we did have fun, it was short lived ending the game session after a little over an hour. We enjoyed our time with the game but there is really only so much fun you can have with a game where the only objective of it is to get to the top of one of 260 randomized mountains.
260!?? Yes you heard right. There are over 260 mountain combinations to race on. The game does offer up a bit of variety in that way. There are three different game modes dividing up the mountains. Classic is probably where you wanna start if you're new to the game. Hard is your next option after that. The most difficult type of mountains generate spinning wheels to make getting to the top even harder.... or easier depending on your skill level. Along with a multitude of mountains you and up to three of your friends can choose from five different available frogs. Neither is better than any other. They are simply different so that you can differentiate between which player is who. If you want to kick it up a notch you can choose to turn on a list of four game modifiers. These include the following:
Only One Arm - Players only have one arm... I mean come on, what did you expect?
Low Gravity - Player's jumps and leaps are more floaty.
Burning Hands - Players will lose their grip if they stay on a grip for too long.
King Of The Hill - The Player in the lead gets points. The player with the most points at the top of the mountain wins.
My favorite thing about the game is how well it controls. Actually controlling your slippery friend can take a few rounds to get used to but once you have the controls down you realize that the game controls almost flawlessly. The fact that it does control so well may be why I actually found myself more interested in the single player mode after playing with friends. When you play solo you are racing yourself (and others on the leaderboard) to the top of the mountains. Every time I plummeted off the map or missed a landing I knew it was my own fault. That is how the game hooked me. I knew I could shave off much more time if only I could get a good launch off the starting line. Each time I reached the end I was either shy of beating my own score by milliseconds or just barely beating my previous record. After retrying only about a million times, I was able to get my time down from 01:05 to a nice 00:42. It really was addicting.
All in all my friends and I really enjoy this game. I'm afraid that other gamers may not give it a fair shot, because of the lack of online connectivity. The game handles perfectly, its fun to play with friends IRL and provides a good challenge when playing solo but in today's age where everything needs to be connected I'm not sure how others will take to it. I recommend giving it a shot.
Frog Climbers is set to release on steam on October 6th and will be 30% off for the first week selling at $4.89 then remaining at the standard price of $6.99.

Legends of Eisenwald is said to be a Medieval Strategy RPG. On the surface it looks even better than I expected it to be. I mean, we are starting to see a lot of good-looking Early Access games, but still it surprises me. I do like myself a good tactics game as most of you well know, so I wasn’t about to pass this opportunity up.
The main pull for myself to Legends of Eisenwald was the combat. That’s also the first disappointment as well. It’s on a hex system, but there’s not as much depth to the combat as I was hoping, but it is rather brutal and fast… kind of like a medieval skirmish would be I presume. You’ve got rear healers and buffs, then your ranged and then your “tanks”. I use air-quotes because as of writing this, really only my main dude is a tank. Everyone else is more like a meat-shield. You can either start to attack the top half or the bottom half with your main character if he’s in the middle as is the default, but everyone else just kind of moves forward to the guy closest to him. This is the fight. You can’t have everyone just jump to one guy at the beginning of the fight, but rather you are forced to fight the closest opponent. If realism was the intention, they got because that does make the most logical sense. Tactics-wise… you can’t change the positioning of your guys before the fight, but rather before you even enter the fight and see how they are aligned and then it’s too late. There are no obstacles, just people and it feels like a different combat system would have worked better here. Maybe a 2.5D isometric combat system?

The story is that you leave your home to go off somewhere and fight only to come back home and find that there is infighting at home. Lame, but dems the brakes. The writing and story in Legends of Eisenwald is pretty solid. I’ve enjoyed most of if not all that I’ve encountered so far. It’s both interesting and intriguing but it seems to be held back by the game proper. The quest log is somewhat useful, but not very. I was once told to go to the southern bridge near a watch tower… there wasn’t one. It will guide you to some places, but not all (which is fine, I can read, but still). You also don’t have too much money, but you’re told to go and hire people to help you out. They cost money per day, but that didn’t come off as obvious to me and I still don’t really see it anywhere listed. The button just says hire not pay this amount each day. (Goodbye money.)
Legends of Eisenwald doesn’t feel too much like your traditional RPG either where you can go off and explore, killing bad guys for loot and money and generally getting the lay of the land. You need more money and I’m believing that is only going to happen while following the story. There is nothing wrong with a linear game, but Legend of Eisenwald doesn’t feel like it was intended to be that way. It gives the feeling like it was supposed to be more open. Maybe you just have to pay your dues and follow the story for it to open up to you later, but that’s not really how I play RPG’s. I wonder off and kill bad-guys and take their money… but the bad guys are mostly broke here.
Score: Wait For Some Updates
I don’t give this score lightly. I really wanted to give Legends of Eisenwald the better of the two impression scores, but while it has a lot of potential, I feel it will probably be more worth it after a few more updates. I enjoyed the story. If they wouldn’t call it a tactics game, I probably would have enjoyed the combat more. The music was good. The overall game as a whole just feels like it’s missing something, maybe it’s better direction (please don’t read that as hand-holding), but when you’ve done a decent job running around questing, but can’t quite figure out how to turn in some of them and run yourself into a place where your only real option is to start over completely… I’m just not a fan. I’ll keep checking on this game and let you know if my opinion changes, but as of right now Legends of Eisenwald I feel like it’s a solid “wait”. Unless you like what they are presenting and want to support them in their endeavor that is (which is completely understandable.)

So, what are my thoughts on this game? Well, it's definitely good. But that's from a fan's point of view, especially considering I played their old game; Discord Times, and loved that just as much. So from an analytical view of the game, what do I think?
Gameplay
The gameplay is quite interesting. You have troops you can hire for gold, but they don't cost much due to castle support. This essentially tells you how many troops you can support without paying them. Then you have the mercs. Troops you can hire for a bit more gold, but you have to pay them per day to keep them around. Expensive, but they can be high level units or simple peasants, so you get what you pay for with them.
- Equipment
Equipment is definitely interesting, but you should know the scale of things. The better it is, the more gold it costs. However, the market you get them at does have an effect. Purchasing equipment at a merchant pier will cost you loads more gold than if you purchase it at a rural market, but this also affects the quality of the items. Merchant piers cost a ton for their items, but their often high quality, and really powerful in your effort for domination while rural markets aren't as costly, but the quality is lower too. However, it's not so low as to completely dismiss it, for a fight can be won with a simple pitchfork, if the odds are close.
- Units
Talking about equipment and such and yet not covering the units? What kind of monster am I? The units are simple and basic at first glance. Recruits, hunters, female healers (I've forgotten their names) and religious men. That about covers it. However, each unit can upgrade a number of times. Recruits can become veteran pikemen or infantry sargents, hunters can become hard hitting crossbowmen or incredibly nasty sargent archers, and the religious lot can become incredibly useful at healing or buffing your other units, if you choose to send them down that route. Each unit can be manipulated and upgrades to your desire. I nearly forgot the nobleman however. He's the unit that you want to upgrade for knights, paladins and other very nasty units. However, due to being noble blood, he costs an utter fortune for healing, and upgrading him takes a fair while, and a lot of effort.
- Story
I can't really say much about it, other than it's quite good, and each action that happens in the storyline, as well as for your character itself makes sense. I won't spoil any of the storyline since it's quite good, but I will tell you this much: Your actions define this story. It's not a simple walk in a park down a narrow hallway, you have options. Be sure to pick what you think is right.
Overall scores
Gameplay: 8/10 - Could definitely be improved in some areas, but at face value, it's definitely good.
Visuals: 7/10 - The game looks quite pretty but I do notice some performance issues in heavy forest.
Sound: 9/10 - This is truly brilliant music in my opinion. The opening music is fabulous and the sound effects fit in with every swing of a sword. Small improvements could be made to where each sound happens but other than that, spot on.
Story: ?/10 - It's a really good storyline, with multiple branching areas and different ways you can do things. It's truly brilliant.
Final score: 8.5/10 - Due to this still being an early access game, there will be errors and issues abound. I've run into several crashes over the course of the development, and it's annoyed me every single time. But talking with the developers and their view for this game, they are definitely working on it. I hope this turns out to be a brilliant game on release!

I went into this Early Access game made by a development studio i had not heard of unsure about its content and a bit skeptical about its quality, but soon after I began playing all these doubts were put to rest. I suddenly found myself deeply submerged into the game and all it has to offer. Legends of Eisenwald is a true strategic RPG game that skillfully combines the heroic elements of  old-school role-playing with tactical turn-based combat and presented in a medieval setting filled with unique legends and folklore.
In this game players will create their hero from a selection of three initial classes and then recruit a small army to travel throughout the realm fulfilling quests, investigating myths and legends, and conquering castles among other things. LoE is still very much Early Access and there will certainly be more changes made. However, this game is entertaining and playable in its current state and offers a lot of nice features.
One of the most interesting features in this game is the concept of changing how the turn-based combat takes place. Unlike other games, Legends of Eisenwald has decided to remove movement points from combat in order to streamline it and make it more dynamic. I like knowing that one strategic movement or action can ultimately determine the outcome of a battle regardless of strength or numbers. Of course, there are lots of weapons, items, and spells typical to any RPG game that will also aid your army in battle. There is also an upgrade tree for improving your units as they gain experience along the way. The user interface is minimal and easy to use. Gameplay speed can be adjusted and there is an option to auto-play battles at any time. The developers have even included a level editor that will allow more content to be added by the community.
Being Early Access also means that the game still has a few drawbacks though. There are still a few bugs in the game so I recommend leaving auto-save enabled or save your game often. The game includes a function to send error reports and crashes directly to the developers when a bug is encountered. However, this is also somewhat buggy and does not always work as intended. Also, the game still lacks the lustrious shine that a finished product has. While the artwork and graphics are very nice and full of detail, there is still no "wow" factor when it comes to battle animations. There is a ton of lore in this game that is scripted well, but the english translation is not very good  and can be confusing to read at times. One would think that this would have been picked up and sorted out through the beta testing community but currently it has not. Some voice acting would also enhance this game tremendously, but i'm not sure it is even being considered. Still, this game is an overall delight and it will definitely improve before its final release.
Legends of Eisenwald is an entertaining game overall and considering its still in Early Access beta there is still a strong possibility that the game will be even better upon completion. While it still needs a lot of polishing and there are still a few scattered bugs in the coding, I still enjoyed it tremendously and would recommend it to fellow strategy/RPG gaming fans. With the right adjustments and improvements this game could become an instant classic.

It's early to write a review, so I might be back to edit this with further impressions! Nonetheless, I'm glad I got the game at release; it feels a little less polished in terms of aesthetics than the first game, but there's new stuff to enjoy -- I really like the holding stations as an addition, because they provide for planning ahead and really tweaking how patient people are (instead of a one-time payment to boost people's patience permanently).
One downside is that your own restaurant feels a little aimless at the moment; I find the chef for hire levels much more interesting (and challenging, because you don't just get to pick the food that you've memorised and are good at). And I do miss some of the movements involved in making food/doing chores in the first game -- they helped differentiate the foods a bit more. I miss soup, for example.
I appreciate design decisions made like not having upgradeable foods -- it means you only have to learn how to do something once, instead of having to adjust your process after you've already got it good and memorised. It does take away from some of the sense of progression, though.
Nonetheless, I'm really happy with it so far, and I love how responsive the dev is to bugs and suggestions. I know there's already plans to do more with your own restaurant levels, add more achievements, etc, etc.
As with the first game, I far prefer it with a controller. I'm just not good at keyboard gaming, and all the different key binds were difficult to learn. I just use my PS4 controller and it works great.
So I already recommend it, but it's going to get better.
Edit: Realised I've mostly compared this to the first game, so if you don't know the first game... at the moment, I'd recommend playing that first. It has a lot of the same stuff, it's currently cheaper, and it's a finished product. I enjoy the time management and memorisation the games require; if that doesn't sound like your thing or you'd get stressed about the quick onslaught of things to learn and do, it probably wouldn't be great.

I enjoyed this game and I'll probably revisit it a few times in the coming days to get all the achievments. Heres my personal breakdown of the game.
PROS:
- The game does a fairly good job of creating a simple story with no real dialogue
- The 2D sprites are rather nice, and everything looks pretty good
- There is no filler to this game, no real padding. Everything that happens is there for a reason
- Your actions can actually influence (albeit slightly) the outcome of the game
- The fact that you grow as you gather powerups is a nice touch
PRO/CON:
- The flight mechinism takes a bit to get used to. If you try to 'flap' before you start the downward part of your arc in the air, you won't really get any height. I personally like this, because it makes you feel a bit more like you're actually controlling something thats flying rather then just a double-jump like most platformers. Still, some won't care for it, so I can't just list it as a 'pro'.
- I will admit... the main reason I bought this is because I LOVE games where you can play as a dragon. Not only play as one, but play as one thats not EVIL.
- While I admire the 2D sprites the hand drawn pictures are... meh. Certainly better then I can draw off hand but I feel that they could have been a bit more polished looking. They aren't poorly drawn or distracting but they're not fantastic either.
CONS:
- Although there are no fillers, the game is very short. It took me about an hour to beat from start to finish. This is honestly the only thing that I found disapointing.
- It's not immeidatly obvious that you can effect the outcome of some situations. If it weren't for the fact there are achievments for it, I wouldn't have thought I could change anything.
Its not a perfect game but I'm very satisfied with it. Its fun, charming, and I hope the developer makes more dragonic games in the future.

A KickStarter game.
Archeblade was a game with massive goals. It looked, and sounded amazing. Sadly though the project fell through only because of one simple fact, they had no one to market the game. It's still somewhat alive, not a broken game really at all. You can't hack the game at all to my knowledge, just map a key to register it to the debug console. Which...Works...In..Multiplayer.. Oh well. The game's graphics are very decent and so are the characters, they had a mind to atempt to go for something very forwarded to a Japanese fighter styled game. To me it felt like Mortal Combat meets Call of Duty. There's shotguns, snipers, pistols and revolvers, don't forget the katanas, bows and arrows, magic and more. It's a very fun game with tons of hours of replay ability even more so for the fact you can't one wolf it. The team games absolutely require the need for cooperative action. The good news is that it's not forced so dramatically that you need a good team to win. Not at all, just keep to your combos and help your team. It's like a game of Domination. Sadly though this game was scrubbed, all because of poor marketing.... Even though I love the game dearly, expect the community to die off very soon.

Сиквел драматически уступает первой части игры по следующим причинам:
1. Проблемы  с вариативностью
- Больше нет апгрейдов продуктов для ресторана
- Больше нет сложных рецептов (как суп или головоломный шиш-кебаб), даже опционально
- Больше нет необычных рецептов (навроде жареных бананов с их таймингом)
- 70% рецептов ОЧЕНЬ простые, в 2-3 кнопки.
- 70% рецептов полностью одинаковые.
Рекламные заверения про 180+ видов еды - профанация. Если скоратить однообразную еду, ее будет меньше, чем в оригинале. Причем никто не написал на сайте игры, где представлен список из 180 блюд: "ребята, меню выглядит отлично, но реально рецептов тут 10-15 от силы!".
2. В игре есть баги, недоработки, плохие шрифты, отключенные возможности (ибо сломаны). Такое ощущение, что игра находитя в раннем доступе, только нас снова не предупредили.
3. По сюжету, протагонист теряет все, что он создал в первой части игры. Но он не сдается, собирает свои сбережения, чтобы создать и развить новый ресторан. Арендовав помещение и открыв свое заведение он начинает бегать по десятку чужих баров и клубов, работая там поваром.
Где логика?
4. Развития и целей в игре нет.
- Нет кампании со своим рестораном (только свободная игра)
- Нет наград за прохождение чужих заведений
- Улучшать и покупать нечего (а то, что обещают в обновлениях, уступает первой игре)
- Ачивки в стиме сделаны "на отцепись". Они незамысловатые по условиям и все выглядят одинаково! Даже на иконки времени не нашлось.
-  Заработанные в игре деньги тратить некуда (кроме одинаковых блюд)

5. В игре есть серьезные недостатки. Но, что мы видим в превью обещанного обновления? Может быть новые блюда и челленджи? Может бысть развитую систему апгрейдов, не уступающую предшественнице? Балансировку сложности? Нормальные ачивки?
Нет. 140 новых ни на что не влияющих предметов для кастомизации ресторана.

6. Игра потеряла шарм своих истоков. Нет веселого лора (как с древним кланом ниндзя в первой части), интерфейс жуткий (но при старте был еще хуже), музыка не запомнилась.
И напоследок. Когда я написал подобные вопросы разработчику в теме (про отсутствие прогресса и странности сюжета), счачала мне отвечали, что "все будет в обновлениях", а потом забанили.

The strength of Thief to me lies in the ability to edit the setting of the difficulty level. Play on the hardest difficulty and turn off the reticle, turn on zero damage meaning you can't fight even if you wanted to, make resources more expensive, turn on no alerts meaning you fail if you are spotted and play it on Iron man mode if you want a really difficult experience. These plus a number of other modifiers are what make the game good in my opinion. They also give you extra points for playing the game with these on so you can rack up good scores if that's what you are after.
If you also feel like it, turn off the HUD as well such as mini-map, health bar, Threat icons etc. It makes the game have a huge amount of options and variations which could potentially give it loads of replay value and challanges.
The rest of the game is good, lighting is bloody nice and the stealthing is pretty fun. PC port is also very well done so big props for that.
Mainly though to me the selling point is the amount of fun that could be had with the ability to edit the diffculty and make it a truely challenging stealth game.

Having played Magic for around 18 years now. Including all of the pc games. This just handles so much worse then everything else ive seen.
I'm not talking about the game here, MTG has been around since forever and it's great for what it is. It's just the UI, the forced Tutorial, the slow animations. Just a few examples of what got my blood boiling here.
-Continue turns into the skip attack button, im sure thats not going to cause problems for people
-Sometimes spacebar activates the top button, sometimes the bottom one, sometimes nothing. Shortcuts, anyone?
-Having to sit there watching the clock go through every phase, every attack damage done, every slow animation and whatever stupid tutorial tip the game throws my way just to sit up, move my mouse, click one button, and then watch nothing again for a waaaay tooo long of a time. And how dare you trying to make a play while we show the 10th creature doing 1 damage.
-With such a slow system you are sure you are making the play you want right? Well cards get played with a single click and at least for me didnt light up (select) proper so be careful.
If you want Magic, stay with MTGO, if you want a single player campaign there have been plenty of Magic Games who did a better job. Hell even Shandalar was better which was released almost 20 years ago.
If you want an example for a modern card game, look at Heartsthone, the game is fun to just handle. The cards have a real feel to them, it's fun to slam them on the board, i can finish my turn before the first animation finishes even though the animations are so much quicker then these are. This being Magic it's harder but please, at least a single phase could be smooth.
Stay away, i was surprised when i saw this because i didnt see a need that this would satisfiy and im right, it's just someone trying to turn a licence into a f2p cash cow. With the least amount of effort possible.
Shame on anyone involved in this. Shame.

I have always been a fan of racing games, playing titles from NFS to GRID to DiRT to Forza, Nascar, and more. For PC, I must say that the GRID series, minus the first game, is phenomenal. GRID 2 deviates from its prior by balancing simulation-level damage and graphics with arcade-style racing. While there are a few things that were missed, such as an in-car view, the huge selection of vehicles, tracks, and environments make this game really stand out.
GRID 2 has a fantastic storyline. You are a new driver, trying to make a name for yourself and your racing league, WSR. You're led by the confident Patrick Callahan, who keeps you up to date on promo events, passing in races, and reminding you of sponsor objectives. The game is split into "seasons," with each season taking place in a different region. At season 4, you race at tracks globally. In general, each season means a new tier of cars, but there is some overlap, making seasons 3 and 4 both T3 races. There are difficulties suitable for anyone, from racing newcomers to GRID experts. There are multiple race types, such as Endurance, Time Attack, Overtake, Drift, Race, Touge, and more, all of which are very enjoyable. The only caveat I find with any of the game modes is when playing Touge, the aggressiveness of your opponent will count against you, even if they hit you. Just avoid aggresion in this mode, and you'll be fine.
The GRID 2 community is alive and well, and the forums are still relevant. Performance is great online, and you can upgrade your cars to suit your own driving style. If I remember correctly, multiplayer lobbies can go up to 12 players at once, but please correct me if I'm wrong. Even when you beat the Single Player Campaign, you will still have loads of fun in online multiplayer.
One of the things that I look for in a game is whether or not it is enjoyable to play a second time, after you beat it once. I must say that this is one area where this game excels. I often found myself retrying races with different vehicles to beat my lap times, rise in the leaderboards, or just to see the difference each made.
GRID 2 supports a wheel & pedals setup, but I simply use a keyboard. While there are disadvantages to doing so, i.e. pressing W is equivalent to going pedal-to-the-metal 24/7, the steering is very managable and drifting is easy to pick up on. The graphics are fantastic. I don't quite know what graphics engine this game runs, but I play the game on Ultra settings at 50-60 fps on a GTX 860M. It's optimized incredibly well, and lighting, shadows, and reflections all look great. You certainly won't have weather effects anywhere near games such as Project CARS or Assetto Corsa, but the game will be just fine for the vast majority of players.
I purchased GRID 2 on Steam during the 2015 Summer Sale, but I did have it installed previously. Feel free to add about 15 hours to my Steam timelog for it to make up for this. You can pick it up for USD $7.50 as of writing during this "North Pole Noir" sale, and you certainly won't regret it. There are  number of DLC packs, all of which I personally do own but don't use very often. I feel like Codemasters hit the sweet spot with the DLC attractiveness, as there are plenty of cars in the base game that will outperform the DLC vehicles, but some of the DLC packs offer more vibrant patterns. For example, the base game's T3 Honda will outperform the T3 DLC Camaro SS, but the Camaro SS is a fantastic looking car. The reloaded edition of this game is probably the best deal you will get, at least when it is on sale.
Not only is GRID 2 the best racing game in its class, the unique storyline makes up from something looked over in most racing games. If you love racing games, you will love this!
Be sure to check out any of my other reviews on my profile, and please upvote if this helped you, I hope it did! Also, I have a few screenshots from this game posted! Thanks for reading!

TL;DR. A nice arcade like game in a small well executed package. Sober but functional both in the graphics and sound department.
If you like the old arcade games that are based on some good solid gameplay, then look no further. Your new match made in heaven has just arrived...
Mr. Shifty is a pure action based game, that relies on skill and not on some cheesy Random Number Generator. This means that the action of the opponents can be predicted and that you can learn the patterns of the game. This is especially useful in the end stages were there is a lot of spawning of new enemies, but he player can learn the patterns making it less of a twitch game then a RNG should otherwise make of it.
The stages are divided in nice small levels, so that in case of dead you simply restart the latest level. Thus avoiding possible replays of several dull (or particularly difficult) sections is thus nicely avoided. This small piece-by-piece approach also makes for 'just one more try'-addiction.
Over the course of the 18 stages new gameplay mechanics are introduced. This avoids the dreaded over-and-over-again repetition that most action games fall victim to.
Game is not too long (my first play through was +/- 7 hours), but has some decent replay value.
The story is nothing special but serves it purpose of gluing the stages together. The music fits the action well and is the usual beat music. The graphics are sober, some might say even bland, but they help the gameplay by making it easy to distinguish al the onscreen items.

Great atmosphere, good art style, quite a lot of characters with different stories and background, and I love the music. The decisions you make in the game affect your characters mood / health. Sometimes it feels a bit slow, especially the stories that take 40+ days; but I think it adds to the atmosphere, the fact that you don't know how long it'll take this time or how hard the winter is gonna hit.
Surviving is not that easy with sickness, injuries, sadness, depression, hunger, tiredness and crime all over the place. Some locations are quite eiree.
Overall it's a great experience full with difficult decisions and choices. It may have very small glitches from time to time, but nothing too bad.

Frog Climbers is a silly, fun and well-polished physics racing game.
The objective of the game is to be the first player to reach the top of the mountain. You have control over both your hands, and aim them using the analogue sticks of your controller, similarly to games like Octodad or Mount your friends.
You then use your triggers to grasp onto a ledge or rock. (An important note is you can not play this with a keyboard or mouse).
The game does a good job at keeping the game fun for all players. A lot of racing games suffer from the problem that as soon as someone gets the lead, the players in the back will never be able to catch up, and so they don't have as much fun. In Frog climbers, occasionally a bug carrying a vine will fly next to losing players, which if they grab will then get a boost upwards. If players fall off the mountain, they will also respawn after 3 seconds near the player in first place. Although it seems they can fall as many times as they want, as I haven't seen some sort of penalty. I would personally like to see a life limit or something along those lines.
Something pretty hilarious is you have the ability to grab other frogs' limbs. You can grab their feet, knees, hands or backs. It will weigh them down slightly, and you can use them to swing or climb up. However, there is a timer where your frog will lose grip after a while to keep it from getting to frustrating for other players.
Although if you don't like the idea of being able to catch up and win at the last second, you can turn on a modifier that will reward the player who has the lead, which will then be compared across all players once the end is reached. There are other funny modifiers to play around with like low gravity or one arm. As well as choosing modifiers, you can also generate a map type of normal or hard difficulty, or even a map filled with wheel obstacles for extra challenge.
The map generation is quite similar to the one in many worms games, except instant, which is quite nice.
You can choose between 5 different types of frogs, which could easily just be different colours, but I like that the devs took the time to give them different body shapes, patterns and such. The green one plays upside down, and climbs with their feet instead, which I found to be quite funny.
You can also race in solo against the clock in preset, daily mountains in order to try get a higher score on the leaderboard.
My main issue with the game is there's no AI, and no online play, which means you can only really have fun in the game if you have friends over. Sure you can play solo, but I don't think that would keep you entertained for a very long time. So it's definitely a multiplayer game.
Overall, I think the game is super fun. It's a simple idea, but very well executed! There's a decent amount of content for the relatively cheap price, and if you have friends over, it's definitely a fun game to start up and have a few good rounds. Although I'm all for local multiplayer, I hope the devs consider putting in AI or most importantly, online play in the future.
Still, great time!

This is a fantastic racing game, with an almost perfect balance between fun and realism. On my mid-range system (Linux, i5-6400, GTX 750ti) it runs very well at 2560 x 1080 on very high graphical settings.
While there are certainly a few minor negatives (most serious is the absence of pitstops, but also things like the inability to save replays, the limited range of speech effects, some graphical shortcuts and a couple of program crashes while navigating the menus), the positives easily outweigh them.
There's a great range of racing modes, vehicles and locations, which are enhanced even further if you pick up the DLC packs. Open Wheel, Street and Touring are particularly impressive, while Drag racing (via DLC) and the Demolition Derby add even more variety.
You can easily customize the difficulty based on your skill (AI quality, driver aids), and there's a good progression from easier to very challenging racing based on the vehicle class and tracks you race on or the competition you enter. There's a full range of interior and exterior views, great handling mechanics and, above all, an amazing sense of sheer speed as you take a sequence of corners surrounded by AI cars.
A very nice career mode is the main focus, but you can always set up a quick race, customized to your liking or go online to race against fellow gamers.
If you like racing games at all, get this one.

Short version:
This game is amazing, the mechanics are perfect and the levels are challenging enough. The only downside is that it desperately needs an endless mode.
Long version:
This is my very first review to a game but I felt this game really deserves the recommendation. This became one of my favourite games of all time and the reason for that is pretty simple: the developers had an idea for a game and they built everything around that idea only to serve the gameplay itself.
I want to go through the main parts of the game just to describe what I mean:
- Gameplay:
You can teleport around for short distances while you have to punch people in the face ridiculously fast. It gets challenging as you go from stage to stage but I think it never gets unfair, instead I always felt like I had to be better and faster. Even though the game recommends controller, I played with mouse and keyboard and it still was an amazing experience. The basic mechanics are easy to use but hard to master which means if you don't know exactly what to do in chaotic situations, you will end up shot in the face by somebody, or blown away by a rocket quite regularly. The game will give you new challanges through the whole game which means it didn't become boring to me even though the whole teleporting and punching method won't change during the entire game. If you learn the behaviour of the enemies, you can do amazing things by dodging all the bullets and punching them through the walls.
- Story:
It is almost a parody, its not meant to be taken seriously. The only downside of the game for me is the fact that the story is short and you don't have any options after that but to replay the story again. I think there should be an endless mode with some prebuilt levels and randomly placed enemies.
The statement I wrote before is true here as well: everything is here only to serve the gameplay. As you go along, the story will reveal new challenges and obstacles which obviously will make the game harder.
- Graphics:
You only leave destruction behind you as you go through the rooms. Everything is colorful which means you can easily recognize the different enemy types at the first glimpse. This helps a lot because with the speed of this game you really need to be able to know what to do at the moment you see an enemy. The silhouettes and the very distinct colors of the enemies make this really easy.
- Overall:
The graphics and the story are both there to create a better gameplay experience while the basic mechanics are also entertaining enough on their own. The sounds are amazing, the music is good and every time I dodge an enemy's bullet and then punch him through a wall, I feel myself like the biggest badass in the universe because of how satisfying it feels.

If you're familiar with the game Magical Ride (I believe it's only available to play on Facebook?), the reward/achievement system is very much identical to that. Achievements are very easy to reach but you don't feel under pressure to reach them. Most of them naturally occur during your run/s.
There's gameplay and costume upgrades that you can buy with the screws you've collected as well.
I can't tell what's more relaxing when I play this game, the music, the rotating planets or the sounds that my little astronaut guy is making?
Anyway, super recommended for casual players and/or achievement hunters!

This game makes you feel badass. More than broforce. More than just cause. More than one finger death punch. More than Sleeping Dogs? IDK You don't really think about the shifting, you just watch out for the lazer sights and teleport out. Near the start of the game, when there is a whole bunch of people guarding the door, and you can just press a button to kill all of them, I just teleported into the room and beat them all up. It's not like you are over powered, you can only shift five times, and each has a regen of a half a second. But if you get to 0 shifts, it takes a couple seconds to regain them. So it is rewarding if you stratigically shift, rather than blindly. Punching comes down to button mashing, but you could probblably take out two people with just punching. I wished there was a system where if you landed the first punch, and kept the button held, it would throw a second, then third. That would make wall punching worth your time. But with shifting and then punching, you can take out as many people as you like, as long as they are the brain-dead type. AI is pretty dumb... I mean, you can see each person working through their path-finding algorythem. And if you punch a wall while they come at you, they freeze for a second.
The story is dumb, but on pourpose. Stone can't stop thinking about how evil he is, the secritary or whoever is all like "girl power" and Mr. Shifty is scilent. This game does not have the "restart, try a new method" system like other games... which I like, but I KID YOU NOT the slow mo bar is the dumbest thing I have came across. It should be like a second life, where you can get hit a second time... but no. It is only if a bullet A BULLET gets even close to you. There is some levels that take longer because you have a full bar at the begining, and you aren't even rewarded with more time while in slow mo. And after slow-mo, YOU CAN'T EVEN GET MORE UNTIL AFTER TWO SECONDS. You can get back your slow-mo after just running into a room and beating everyone up, but that goes agenst the enforced gameplay.
There is one thing however, that is the best... the door kicking. I have recently bought doorkickers and action squad, and played hotline miami 2 and gunpoint a while back... And this is by far the best door kicking in a game ever. You can direct where the door will go based on where you are standing and what direction you are facing. The one problem, is that the door will not auto close like a normal door after you open it. (I think hotline miami does this.)
So this game gets a 7.5 out of ten. About the same as broforce. The combat is sooo good, but what I hate the most in a game is when you die and it's not your fault. Sometimes it's like, I pressed the wrong button, but in this game, the heavies sometimes punch wayy too fast, and sometimes the grenade goes off in your hand when in other games, like in HL2 deathmatch it resets the timer. I don't know why this is one of the game awards nominees. Heat Signature is my GOTY, but didn't evenn get nominated.

Dragon's Wake presents a unique perpective of the sterotypical "knight slays the dragon" story. In the meantime, it created a series of relatively new control scheme for the indie platforming genre.
The controls are admittedly terrible on the keyboard, but all of that gets fixed pretty quickly if you plug in a controller. With a controller, the rather unusual controls are actually quite fun and satisfying.
While the graphics could use some tightening up, the music and sound effects worked well to give you that sense of adventure.
Dragon's Wake aslo does a really good job of telling a heartfelt story without the use of a real verbal or written narrative. Everything in the story is shown to you through action and choice, which makes you feel more invested in it.
Probably the biggest drawback is that this game is extremely short. There is a good ending and a bad ending which helps  expand Dragon Wake's lifespan, but it still takes no more that a few hours to finish twice. If you're looking for a game to experience for an evening, then this game is fine, but if you're looking for something to fill out your weekend, then this may not be the right choice.
Overall, I did end up enjoying this game. The devs do some neat things here, and I'd love to see what they can come up with next.

Dragon's Wake is a game about a dragon and his reptillian buddies - ostensibly kobolds - trying to survive. As someone who likes both dragons and kobolds, perhaps more than could be considered healthy, it was a snap buy at the price point, and it was well worth the money.
Let me get this out of the way: The game is very short - I'd estimate somewhere between 2 and 2.5 hours for a first playthrough and subsequent ones could likely cut that in half. The game has a little replayability (finish it, then go look at the achievements you missed, realize there might be a better ending, and go play it again), but overall I wouldn't expect to get more than 5ish hours of playtime out of this title. That said, it's $3.59, at full price. You can't go wrong.
The story is delivered through images on loading screens, which works well - there's no speech or text, and none is needed. There were a few weird inconsistencies between these images - the kobolds, for instance, seem to go back and forth between having tails and not a few times, which was a little off-putting, but it's a minor complaint.
As a platformer, it does a pretty decent job. The controls feel tight, though it could have stood to be a bit longer, and it could use a bit more enemy variety. There are only a couple bosses, and the difficulty ramps up considerably for the final encounter. To give some perspective, I didn't even come close to dying until the final fight, then died ~10 times before winning. Difficulty isn't a bad thing by any means, but it didn't feel like a ramp so much as running into a wall.
I encountered no bugs, which is always nice.
All of that said, it's a game worth playing, especially if you like riding emotional roller coasters. If it was a $10+ game, I would have a difficult time recommending it, but at $3.59, I absolutely do.

Great game. Easy to use interface makes learning the prestigious strategy fun, and easy. I've noticed these guys are doing their best, but their game needs more work which will take more man hours, and sadly more funding which is a challenge with a free to play game. They do have a in game store you can transfer credit from a steam account. In my honest opinion the microtransactions are worth it. If nothing else it's charity for the builders of the game. Me personally? In my honest opinion trying to build a deck with the bare bones is grueling. It's not undoable; however it does take away from the joy I get from building a deck I have in my head, and testing it on strangers, and fine tuning it. The max offer for their micro currence is $40 which is less than a typical game, and the boosters from the set you choose are guaranteed each time to increase your collection size by a certain percentage.
It also doesn't ruin the card game itself. If anything it gives me the chance to test my decks out before I challenge opponents with my real deck which mirrors (More or less) my virtual decks. It's also nice that you can reuse the same card in different decks without having to take a deck apart which for me as a deck builder is important. With the deck builder setting up ratios is easy (Just wish it had a search bar to look up specific cards), but it does have a very nice filter to narrow down things like the color (Colorless, and Non-color cards too), enchants, creatures, instances, sorcery's, and lands.

CSD2 should offer plenty of fun for fans of the original. Unlike other reviewers here, I prefer this entry's more streamlined approach to cooking, which facilitates quicker gameplay and mitigates the frustration of juggling complex recipes. And the music and visuals prove as charming as ever.
However, CSD2 remains inferior to its predecessor in many ways---at least in its present state. In an apparent attempt to lessen the tedium associated with CSD1's campaign mode, the developer opted for a more freeform system, giving the player access to a myriad of recipes from the outset as well as the option to work for other restauraunts in the "Chef for Hire" mode. Unlockables come in the form of new recipes, restauraunts, and decorations and furnishings. Unfortunately, the absemce of catering events, kitchen upgrades, and in-game story elements (such as food inspections and dating) all contribute to a perceived lack of progression from the player's perspective. This also leaves CSD2 feeling rather barebones in comparison to CSD1, despite the abundance of additional features. But the developer has expressed willingness to implement further, substantive content, and I have full confidence in his abilities and commitment.
My criticisms notwithstanding, CSD2 still deserves praise for what it accomplishes in terms of core gameplay. Complaints about a clunky UI and lack of mouse support (which the developer has promised to address) feel a bit excessive, since I did not have any trouble navigating my way through the menus. I have encountered no bugs beyond minor issues with lower framerates and graphical glitches. As it turned out, the game automatically runs off of integrated graphics; switching to my dedicated graphics card resolved everything.

This is a clever variation on match 3 puzzle games; you control a team of characters, and you beat up the other team by making matches. Each character does different amounts of damage from different colors, and every character has three unique abilities which mesh to create the gameplay.
The problem is that this is a free to play game, and it is one of those free to play games which is constructed entirely around exploiting the darkest parts of the human psyche. It is all about addiction, trying to get you to keep playing to keep getting more slots for your heroes, and it is just a tremendously addictive exerience as you're always short of having enough slots for all your characters - and if you don't put your characters into a slot, you lose them.
This is designed to compel you to keep playing, and manipulate you into playing far more than the game actually warrants.
The core gameplay is decent enough, but if you have any addictive tendencies at all, this game will chew you up and spit you out.

R.I.P.D is a third-person, singleplayer/co-op, wave-shooter based on the movie of the same name. The game is as simple as it gets with the key objective of killing every dead minion across five waves of rising difficulty and arrest or execute a mini-boss deado at the very end.  Encounters are a race against time with each minute equalling a player life.  If the player dies a life is deducted.
. Play solo or in co-op with another player.
. Seven maps to play on.
. Eleven weapons to choose from.
. Twelve consumables to purchase from before each encounter.
. A kill bar can be filled that allows the use of five distinct abilties.
. Re-arm weapons from ammo chests.
. Six types of distinct enemies. Some with melee weapons others with firearms.
. Plus special mini-bosses with extra health that must be arrested or executed.
. Earn salary by completing missions, quests and bets.
. Use salary to unlock new weapons, upgrade them or purchase consumables.
. Bets allow you and a friend to compete against each other in one of five optional quests.  The winner receives a multipler to their salary.
. Every win also recovers gold which when enough is earnt unlocks the final mission to face Kevin Bacon's character (from the film.)
+ Nice amount of weapons and consumables to use.
+ Well conceived and implemented player abilities.
+ Great A.I. results in enemies that work very well in groups and to the best of their abilities.
+ Robustedly designed gameplay though short in content actually comes together to provide overall a decent experience.
- In solo gameplay can become ponderous and boring.  Especially as every enemy is gunning for you.  Whereas with another person the threat is split.
- Too few enemy types.  A few more would have been perfect.
- Player respawns are atrocious. Especially on harder levels.
- Gameplay is impossible on harder difficulties unless you have a partner, until you unlock the special weapons.
- Choosing to either Reynolds or Bridges main characters from the film has no special effect.
- Progress not scaled appropriately for solo play.  Gaining salary is very, very slow.
- No one plays this game.  So good luck finding a willing partner.
- Would have liked to have more voice-over/one liners pulled from the movie for both main characters.
* Basic console port. Limited gameplay and controls of console type.
* Three difficulty levels allow for a nice learning curve and eventually decent salary rewards to acquire and upgrade every weapon.
* Well made maps add to the general video and audio ambience.
* Achievments come think and fast at the start but the last three achievements: Win all maps on Hard, earn enough salary to unlock all weapons and max. upgrade all weapons were a bit of a grind.
R.I.PD is well-made but pedestrian to play.  It reminds me alot of the early shoot-em ups you would find in arcades.  Remember those!?  While gameplay is okay, it gets boring pretty fast played solo.  In co-op its less boring and repetitive.  Mostly down to the aspect of trying to out-do each other.  Without another human player you cannot use the betting system which provide a huge boost to salary rewards at the end of each match.
What surprised me was how well the limited numbers of weapons, enemies, maps, challenges and side-bets actually made each session quite varied.  Overall the graphics are visually appealling and the audio is good enough for what is an average title.
Ultimately I walk away from this game feeling its competent but nothing special.  For a movie tie-in its perfectly fine but nothing to sing home about.  If you are a fan of the film it may be worth a look but if you are not a fan of console-style gameplay or have better versions from this genre in your library, you may wish to stick with those.  If you are tempted for the achievement completion, note the final few achievements are a little grindy.

TL;DR Mr. Shifty is a mix of Hotline Miami and Tracer from OW. And this mix works brilliantly elevating an already impressive chaotic and in the same time highly tactical action of HM to even higher level.
Story in this kind of game is not really important. Of course it always adds to the experience, but nailing down the action should be the primary goal. Mr. Shifty can't really go beyond "There's the bad guy, get to him through his goons". There are a few twists and turns, but even they mostly serve the purpose of introducing new gameplay elements.
This is most certainly not the case, as was with HM. It's simple and straightforward, which might actually be a good thing as it focuses on gameplay and it is there where it shines.
The controls are very simple - you can punch, pick up object (and punch with them), and shift (blink if you like). Everything is very fluid and i haven't experienced any sort of clunkiness or glitches.
Music is very generic but it is enough to underline the action. There is a nice touch where music is muffled in a anti-shift field. The sounds are okay, and the cues are just noticeable enough to act on them. It is not the strongest feature of the game, but it works.
The graphics are simple and are not really inspiring. It doesn't subtract from the experience, but might be just a little too little for some. What i didn't like were the cartoony images of a monologue UI. They looked somewhat amateurish. Overall it is not bad and definitely work as you can clearly distinguish different types of enemies and their states.
This is where the game makes it worth it's cost. The fast-paced action and emergent narrative of an encounter are both thrilling and hilarious. You feel very powerful with you little secret weapon, yet it is very easy to make a mistake and catch a bullet with you head. There are a number of different enemies that require different approach and each area feels different too, even though you still do the same routine of punching and blinking.
Another way that the game differs from HM is an inclusion of puzzles, that require you to think and act fast. They are not difficult, but still would kill you 3-5 times before you figure them out. Some people cite repetitiveness, but i can't say that is true. The game is repetitive only if you get stuck in one area and have to replay it again and again. I've been stuck only two times and both involved a mob of melee brutes. They don't pose much of a challenge when there are 2-3 of them, but when it's ten and counting you get easily overwhelmed. The first time it happens just remember that you have several melee weapons at your disposal, that you can use to your advantage. The second time it happened i was clever enough (albeit too late at that) to use rocket-goons to smash their own people while i danced around the mob.
Dance is a pretty good descriptor of what the game feels like. It's a violent ballet of punches and kicks that test your wits and reaction.
I haven't finished the game yet, but i feel i'm very close. As you can see 4 hours is probably enough to finish it. Many would find that upsetting, but i don't see a problem with that. It still has a some kind of replay value via the action itself. I would gladly revisit it just to feel again the rush of adrenaline and tactical blinking.
I haven't encountered any major glitches. Come to think of it no minor glitches too. One time i got stuck in some weird place, and it felt like this was supposed to happen as if it was some kind of trap. And few barely noticeable audio glitches. Apart from that the game runs smoothly and nothing bothers you except you own mistakes.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who liked the gameplay of HM, but wants even faster action. It is unfortunate that this game has only around 15k owners (judging by SteamSpy), as it is a product of high enough quality and awesome entertainment value.

Welcome to a fresh take on an old formula. Much of the strategy takes place before a battle ever begins. Who gets which item, which row to place your units in, and who goes on the flank. Never before has initiative been so important. Support units are no longer a bonus, they are a real strategic necessity.
Notice how every game of M&M or King's Bounty turns into a combat grind that keeps you from finishing the game? You will not get that here. Combat is quick, and you no longer spend half the battle jockeying for position. I don't know about you, but that combat fatigue eventually wore me down, and I always eventually found my desire to play the game diminish as the thought of another half hour battle almost had me in tears.
Enjoy strategy and combat that does not dominate the game. Here you get a well written story, with many hard choices and a real touch of human nature where good and evil are not always easy to distinguish.
The developers care about this game to a degree which sets them apart from most other games. Legends of Eisenwald is a wonderful game, with a compelling story no strategy fan should overlook.

First of all there are many negative reviews due to misrepresentation of the game by developer. Most people assumed that this game is an old school RPG game (as it is announced) and judged accordingly. If you want to categorize a game like this it simply falls somewhere between the Heroes series and Disciples series.
I don’t usually write any reviews on games but in my opinion this one is particularly wronged by too many people. The early access version is 6-8 hours long to beat on first playthrough but there are people who played it like 40-50 hours and then disliked it on so many levels which is odd.
At this stage this game deserves at least a 7 out of 10.
Pros:
-Good graphics
-High quality sound and music
-Good controls and camera mechanics
-Simple yet sufficient tutorial as a part of the campaign
-Good story telling
-Manageable army and battlefield size
-Simple yet fun to play battles.
-Good blend of side quests
-Challenging AI both in strategy map and battles
Cons:
-Some bugs and crashes which may hopefully be fixed before full release
-Quest tracking is very unclear, some won't update as you progress, you have to read through the quest that you are on several times before you can figure out what to do.
-Throws you in too deep and leaves you in the dark too soon.
-Camera can’t be unlocked in strategy map (always fixed on your party)
-no minimap (going between the map and strategy map is tiresome at some point)
-very slow levelling
-Lack of restart level option (VERY important to have.)
Overall most of the cons are agreed upon by too many people but most of them can be fixed, polished or added before the full release of this game. As far as I can track the developer team is highly interested in what people think of their game and active on the Forums. So I believe that they can release a way better final product at the end.
